judged_text: The rewritten public members endpoint applies no upper bound to the user-controlled `limit` param — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is passed straight to `.limit(limit)` — so one request can force serialization of a group's entire membership. Any caller who passes the group-visibility check (including anonymous users for visible automatic groups such as trust_level_0, which contains every user) can send ?limit=999999999 and pull the full member list — every username, name, avatar and last_seen row — in a single response, making bulk user enumeration and response-size/resource amplification trivial. The pre-existing code had the same hole (custom groups dumped all members with no pagination at all), so this is not a regression, but this rewrite of the exact lines governing request size was the point to clamp limit (e.g., max 1000) and it didn't.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the rewritten endpoint sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and passes it directly into `group.users...limit(limit)` with no clamp/max (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`). This allows a caller who can access the endpoint (after `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`) to request an arbitrarily large page size, potentially forcing serialization of an extremely large membership list in one response (resource amplification / bulk enumeration vector). The diff does not add any upper bound or validation for `limit`.
